\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أمين} (amīn)}{أمين (amīn)}]{\ar{أمين} (amīn) — honest, trustworthy}

\label{lesson:AR-C499-amin}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to make angry, then the Arabic for to blame.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أمين}}
\textbf{\ar{أمين}} — \emph{amīn} — \textquotedblleft{}honest, trustworthy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{المحاسب} \ar{رجل} \ar{أمين}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{al-muḥāsib rajul amīn.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The accountant is an honest man.
\end{quote}

It also names a keeper of something: \ar{أمين} \ar{المكتبة}, the librarian.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أمين}} (\emph{amīn}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʾ-m-n}, \textquotedblleft{}to be safe, to trust\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Āmin, safe, which you know, comes from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{amīn}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{amīn}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{al-muḥāsib rajul amīn.} — The accountant is an honest man.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to make angry, then the Arabic for to blame, then say \emph{amīn} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أمين} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Honest, trustworthy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{نزيه} (nazīh)}{نزيه (nazīh)}]{\ar{نزيه} (nazīh) — upright, honest}

\label{lesson:AR-C499-nazih}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to blame, then the Arabic for honest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{نزيه}}
\textbf{\ar{نزيه}} — \emph{nazīh} — \textquotedblleft{}upright, honest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{جدي} \ar{رجلا} \ar{نزيها}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna jaddī rajulan nazīhan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather was an upright man.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{نزيه}} (\emph{nazīh}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-z-h}, \textquotedblleft{}to keep far from what is base\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives nazīh as one who keeps away from what is unseemly.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nazīh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nazīh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna jaddī rajulan nazīhan.} — My grandfather was an upright man.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to blame, then the Arabic for honest, then say \emph{nazīh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{كاذب} (kādhib)}{كاذب (kādhib)}]{\ar{كاذب} (kādhib) — untruthful, false}

\label{lesson:AR-C499-kadhib}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for honest, then the Arabic for upright.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{كاذب}}
\textbf{\ar{كاذب}} — \emph{kādhib} — \textquotedblleft{}untruthful, false\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{الخبر} \ar{كاذبا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna al-khabar kādhiban.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The news was false.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{كاذب}} (\emph{kādhib}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{k-dh-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to lie\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Kādhib is the active participle of kadhaba, to lie, which you know.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kādhib}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna al-khabar kādhiban.} — The news was false.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for honest, then the Arabic for upright, then say \emph{kādhib} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مخلص} (mukhliṣ)}{مخلص (mukhliṣ)}]{\ar{مخلص} (mukhliṣ) — loyal, devoted}

\label{lesson:AR-C499-mukhlis}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for upright, then the Arabic for untruthful.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مخلص}}
\textbf{\ar{مخلص}} — \emph{mukhliṣ} — \textquotedblleft{}loyal, devoted\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{الكلب} \ar{صديق} \ar{مخلص}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{al-kalb ṣadīq mukhliṣ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The dog is a loyal friend.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مخلص}} (\emph{mukhliṣ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-l-ṣ}, \textquotedblleft{}to be pure, to be free of anything mixed\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Mukhliṣ is the participle of Form IV: one whose feeling is pure.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mukhliṣ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{al-kalb ṣadīq mukhliṣ.} — The dog is a loyal friend.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for upright, then the Arabic for untruthful, then say \emph{mukhliṣ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{وفي} (wafī)}{وفي (wafī)}]{\ar{وفي} (wafī) — faithful}

\label{lesson:AR-C499-wafi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for untruthful, then the Arabic for loyal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{وفي}}
\textbf{\ar{وفي}} — \emph{wafī} — \textquotedblleft{}faithful\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{صديقها} \ar{القديم} \ar{وفي} \ar{جدا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṣadīquhā al-qadīm wafī jiddan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Her old friend is very faithful.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{وفي}} (\emph{wafī}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-f-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to fulfil, to keep a promise\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A wafī person keeps their word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{wafī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣadīquhā al-qadīm wafī jiddan.} — Her old friend is very faithful.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for untruthful, then the Arabic for loyal, then say \emph{wafī} again
\end{itemize}
